records.title: Answer stages

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a player submits the correct answer during the no-hint stage, when the game accepts it, then the player earns 5 points and their round score locks.
Given a player solves after Hint 1, Hint 2, or Hint 3, when the game accepts the answer, then the player earns 3, 2, or 1 point respectively.
Given a player remains unsolved after Hint 3, when the round ends, then the player earns 0 points and the game reveals the correct answer.
Given multiple unsolved players, when all unsolved players submit for the current stage, then the game confirms stage results and shows the next hint only to players still unsolved.

Initial content/identity/nomination/suggestion record contract preserved verbatim:
Each content record keeps the prompt, answer, hints, accepted alternatives, and category reference together so each round is deterministic.

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `pair_id` | Unique stable identifier for the word pair. |
| `category_id` | Relationship category identifier. |
| `prompt_word` | Word displayed to players at round start. |
| `target_answer` | Canonical paired answer, held by the server until reveal. |
| `accepted_answers` | Explicit alternative spellings or forms accepted as correct. |
| `hints` | Exactly three ordered, predefined hint strings. |
| `background_id` | Reference to the category’s predefined background asset. |

A player identity record stores the selected entry mode (OpenAI OIDC or guest), the profile reference, generated public alias, leaderboard opt-out, and selected icon. Authenticated profiles are associated with the validated OIDC subject; guest identity persists in the same browser/device until site data is cleared.

Nomination records include the normalized candidate word, nominating player, submission timestamp, moderation status, nomination count, and future-pool eligibility state. A nominated word does not replace the required fields in a playable word-pair record.

Category suggestion records include the submitting player, proposed relationship category, exactly three proposed word pairs, submission timestamp, win-unlock evidence, and review status. Each proposed pair must be completed with the fields above before it can be played. Former provisional MCP ID: FR-WP-004. Replaced at user request with a subject-identifying ID.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the configured final round ends, when players have different total scores, then final standings rank them by total score.

Any player in a room can share its room code or deep link to invite others; a deep link bypasses lobby browsing. Joining as a player requires an available slot under the configured capacity. An invited player who reaches a full room can choose observer mode. Before the game start countdown begins, if a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If player/observer membership or readiness has not changed for 30 seconds before countdown, all players are prompted once for that room version to mark ready; any such change resets the interval. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning. If they mark ready before it expires, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while the holdout remains unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the countdown begins. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins, and a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discoverability. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID. These joins use the same atomic capacity check.

records.title: Lobby discovery and matching

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a discoverable lobby is waiting and has fewer players than its configured capacity, when a player browses lobbies, then the lobby appears as joinable; hidden, full, or started lobbies do not appear as joinable.

Given at least one discoverable lobby has an available player slot, when a player uses quick match, then the service assigns them to the oldest eligible lobby, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID, without exceeding configured capacity. Given none is available, then the player is offered browsing or room creation.
Given a player is in a room, when they share its room code or deep link, then another player can use either invitation to reach the intended room, subject to an open slot.

Given a valid room deep link, when a player opens it, then the game bypasses lobby browsing and checks the room directly. If a slot is open, the player joins; if the room has no open player slot, the invitee is offered observer mode.

Given a room is full and the start countdown has not begun, when a player leaves and at least one observer is waiting, then the observer who entered observer mode earliest becomes the final player in the roster, existing players move up to close the vacancy while preserving their relative order, and any remaining observers stay observers.

Given every player in the room has marked ready, when the final ready state is received, then the game start countdown begins immediately and the player roster locks. If a player leaves after the countdown begins, then no observer or other player is promoted or substituted into that player’s place.

Given all but one player have marked ready, when the room enters the holdout state, then the unready player sees a five-second warning to mark ready. If they mark ready before it expires, the start countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while they remain unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the start countdown begins with the remaining roster locked. If the room has exactly two players, the holdout is not removed and the lobby continues waiting; the countdown does not begin until both are ready.

Given the game start countdown has not begun, when no player/observer membership or ready-state change occurs for 30 seconds, then the game prompts all players once for that room version to mark themselves ready; any membership or ready-state change resets the interval.

Lobby discovery and quick match: Rooms are undiscoverable by default; creator may opt in. Quick match selects the oldest discoverable waiting room with a free seat, then stable room ID. The same atomic capacity-checked join command handles the selection.

Given a player in an active room, when they choose Copy Invitation Link and link creation and clipboard access succeed, the generated inviter-bound link is copied and displayed, with an accessible confirmation.
Given a generated invitation link, when clipboard access is unavailable or denied, the link remains visible for manual copying and an accessible message explains that automatic copying failed.
Given a player requests an invitation, if creation fails or returns no link, no new link is shown or copied, no copy-success confirmation is announced, and an accessible error is shown.

records.body: The room view displays the room code, configured maximum capacity, available player slots, current players, and observers separately. A game cannot start with fewer than 2 players. Any player in the room can invite others by sharing its code or deep link. The room identifies the anchor player. Before the game start countdown begins, when a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If the lobby aggregate has no membership or readiness change for 30 seconds before the start countdown, all players are prompted once for that unchanged state version to mark themselves ready; any membership or readiness change resets the idle interval. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning to mark ready. If they mark ready before it expires, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires in a lobby of more than two players and the holdout remains unready, they are removed and the countdown begins with the remaining roster locked. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins; a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. The room creator has no special readiness or start authority; every player has the same lobby controls. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discovery. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room with a free seat and uses stable room ID to break ties. A 10-second countdown begins when all active players are ready. If a player leaves after countdown begins, nobody replaces them. If fewer than two original players remain when the countdown expires, the game is aborted and the room closes.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a player solves during the no-hint stage, when the round results are shown, then that player can submit a candidate answer nomination; players who solve after any hint cannot nominate from that round.

Given a candidate has fewer than 10 nominations or has not passed moderation, when the answer pool is checked, then it is not eligible for future games. Given it has at least 10 nominations and passes moderation, then it enters the future-eligible answer pool but is not playable until its full curated pair record exists.

Given an actor is not authorized to perform moderation or catalog activation, when they attempt to change moderation status or publish content, then the service rejects the action; every change to nomination count, moderation status, and eligibility is auditable; and content cannot be selected for play until it has passed moderation and is complete in the curated catalog.

Nomination counting: Count unique player profiles per normalized candidate. A profile may nominate a candidate once and submit at most one candidate per eligible no-hint solve. Moderation begins at 10 unique nominations.

Moderation workflow: Roles are Content Moderator and Senior Moderator. At threshold, content enters Pending Review. A moderator other than the proposer approves or rejects with a reason. The proposer may appeal once to a Senior Moderator. Approval alone does not make content playable; the complete curated record must pass validation.
